historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (11-12%) diverges sharply from revenue/EPS CAGR (4-9%) and from owner-FCF CAGR (5.9%) -- equity growth is compounding largely via retained earnings net of buybacks at a book multiple below the market's historical P/E, not via operating growth; not used as the growth anchor for that reason. Separately, owner-FCF CAGR (5.9% both 3yr and 5yr) sits materially below reported-FCF CAGR (7.2%/7.4%): SBC has held a stable ~3.0% of revenue, but as revenue growth itself decelerated post-FY22 (the FY22 $61.6B base included a one-off surge year), a rising share of reported FCF growth reflects the SBC charge growing in step with a slower revenue base rather than operating leverage. selected_growth_rate is deliberately below both revenue_3yr_cagr's headline deceleration signal and equity CAGR's inflated read -- the FY2026 guidance (3-4% local currency) and the structural AI-disruption framing in the qualitative analysis argue for anchoring below trailing averages, not above them.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 guidance (3-4% local-currency growth, adjusted EPS $13.78-13.90) is the anchor, not a floor to grow past quickly: growth recovers gradually toward ~5% as GenAI/agentic bookings partially offset Managed Services softness and federal drag, then settles at a 4% terminal rate for a maturer, AI-disrupted professional-services market. Margins hold flat near FY2025 levels as restructuring savings largely fund AI reskilling rather than drop through.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI transformation spend is a durable tailwind, not a threat -- Accenture wins as the systems integrator of choice for agentic AI rollouts, bookings reaccelerate as FY2027-deferred large deals land, and cost-out savings expand margin toward 18.5%+ while the post-crash multiple (~12x owner FCF) re-rates.
scenario_narratives.bear: The Q3 FY2026 bookings collapse is the leading edge of a genuine structural contraction in the billable-hours model: Managed Services and Consulting hours get automated away over several years, restructuring becomes recurring rather than one-time, and the market caps the exit multiple at 12x for a business facing secular volume and margin pressure.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Accenture is a scale-leading, balance-sheet-pristine professional-services compounder now facing its first genuine test of whether agentic AI structurally compresses the billable-hours economics underlying half its revenue. The Q3 FY2026 crash (shares -18-20% in a day, -50%+ YTD at the low) repriced the stock from a historical ~20x+ owner-FCF multiple to ~12x -- a re-rating this model treats as a real, evidenced finding rather than noise to average away. The base case takes FY2026 guidance at face value rather than assuming a swift reversion to the pre-disruption ~9% historical CAGR, and the probability weights lean more bearish than the house default because management itself validated the concern by cutting guidance mid-year. If the AI-disruption fear proves overstated (bull case), the stock is meaningfully undervalued at the current price; if it is the leading edge of a structural reset (bear case), today's price is still not obviously cheap given a shrinking, margin-compressed exit multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: Agentic AI could compress consulting/managed-services labor hours faster or more permanently than any scenario here models, particularly if large clients begin insourcing AI-augmented delivery

Bookings-to-revenue conversion lags by several quarters, so the FY2027-2028 revenue impact of the Q3 FY2026 bookings deterioration is not yet visible in trailing financials and could be worse than the base case assumes
The accelerated $9B FY2026 acquisition program materially increases integration and capital-allocation risk against a backdrop of decelerating organic growth
US federal spending policy (DOGE-driven contract terminations) is a concrete, ongoing drag on the historically stable public-sector book (~8% of revenue)

A structurally lower exit multiple (bear case caps terminal value at 12x FCF) versus the ~20x+ multiple the market granted pre-crash is itself an unresolved judgment call this valuation must make without a long track record of the market's post-AI-disruption re-rating settling point

inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.5%: large-cap (~$110B), net-cash balance sheet, investment-grade credit, low financial leverage (total debt $5.1B vs $10.2B cash) -- argues for a mega-cap-quality rate near 7.5-8%. Set 100bp above that pure-quality baseline (not stacked further as a second risk charge -- see scenario weights below) to reflect the genuine uncertainty the AI-disruption thesis introduces into revenue durability, which the probability-weighted scenarios already carry in the cash flows; WACC is not re-loaded with a second risk premium on top of the bear-weighted scenario mix.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- operating leases are real-estate office footprint, immaterial relative to FCF; no lease adjustment applied
inputs.notes: Route: standard operating/professional-services owner-FCF DCF (SKILL.md routing table), scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon component build. First valuation of this ticker -- no prior DCF or memory entry exists. FY2026 framed explicitly as a STRUCTURAL repricing, not a one-off trough: Q3 FY2026 earnings (2026-06-18) saw shares fall ~18-20% in a single day on Managed Services bookings down ~15% YoY and a guidance cut (revenue growth ceiling 5%->4% local currency), which the qualitative analysis frames as the market's first large-scale repricing of AI/agentic disruption risk to the billable-hours consulting/managed-services model -- not a cyclical demand air-pocket. Accordingly the base case does NOT mid-cycle-average back toward the 9%+ historical revenue/EPS CAGR; it anchors to FY2026 guidance (3-4% local currency growth, adjusted EPS $13.78-13.90) and decelerates the historical growth rate materially, crediting only a partial, uncertain AI-bookings offset (GenAI revenue tripled to $2.7B in FY25, GenAI bookings ~$5.9B) against the structural bookings headwind. EBITDA margin is held broadly flat to the FY2025 level (~16.9-17.3% mature) rather than assumed to expand on the AI narrative -- operating margin has in fact been remarkably stable at 13.7-15.2% through FY20-25 including the current disruption year, so the base case treats margin resilience as the base rather than the upside. Net cash ($5.0B, Q2 FY2026) is below the 1x-owner-FCF materiality threshold for stripping interest income, but interest income is still stripped as the house-standard treatment applied uniformly across this folder to avoid double-counting the cash pile (added back via net_debt at the end of the DCF). Owner-FCF 3yr/5yr CAGR (5.9%/5.9%) runs materially below reported-FCF CAGR (7.2%/7.4%) -- SBC has been rising as a share of the FCF base (stable ~3.0% of revenue, but revenue growth itself has decelerated since FY22), surfaced in historical_growth.notes. No Extracted/*.txt filings exist for this SEC XBRL-only ticker (ACN/Extracted is empty) -- the component-line greps (lease principal, tax paid detail, dividends KPI) that dcf_context.py normally surfaces were unavailable; all figures were built from ACN_Metrics.csv (core_metrics/XBRL-derived) and ACN_Analysis.json guidance section instead. Cash tax rate held at 24% flat, close to Accenture's historical effective rate band and NI/OpInc-implied retention (~75-78%); no valuation-allowance release or one-off credit distorts the FY2025 base year, so no ramp is required.

bear.narrative: Agentic AI disruption is structural, not cyclical, and Q3 FY2026's 15% YoY Managed Services bookings decline is the leading edge of a genuine, multi-year contraction in the billable-hours economics underlying half of Accenture's revenue -- large clients increasingly automate the work Accenture used to staff, compressing both hours and headcount needed per engagement. Bookings-to-revenue lag means the growth damage shows up over FY2027-2029 even as trailing revenue still looks resilient today. Restructuring becomes a recurring cost of continually right-sizing a shrinking labor-intensive core (further charges beyond the initial ~$865M) rather than a one-time reset, keeping EBITDA margin capped around 15-16% versus FY2025's 16.9%+. Federal spending cuts (DOGE) and large-deal push-outs to FY2027 compound the growth headwind, and the accelerated $9B M&A program adds integration risk against a deteriorating organic base. Terminal growth held at only 2% and the exit multiple capped at 12x reflect a market no longer willing to pay a compounder multiple for a business facing genuine secular margin and volume pressure.

base.narrative: FY2026 guidance (3-4% local-currency revenue growth, adjusted EPS $13.78-13.90) is taken as the true starting point, not smoothed away -- growth recovers modestly toward 5% by year 4-6 as GenAI/agentic bookings (tripled to $2.7B revenue in FY25) partially offset continued softness in Managed Services (bookings -15% YoY in Q3 FY26) and federal drag (DOGE-related contract terminations, ~8% of revenue), then decelerates to a 4% terminal rate reflecting a maturer, AI-disrupted professional-services market. EBITDA margin holds essentially flat to FY2025's ~16.9-17.3% -- the ~$865M restructuring/cost-out program is assumed to roughly fund reinvestment in AI-skilled headcount (80,000+ AI specialists targeted) rather than drop to the bottom line, consistent with margin having been stable 13.7-15.2% operating margin through five years including the current disruption year.

bull.narrative: AI transformation spending proves a durable net tailwind rather than a threat: enterprises need Accenture precisely because agentic AI rollouts across a fragmented multi-vendor stack require a large-scale systems integrator, so GenAI bookings (~$5.9B and rising) convert into a reaccelerating top line as large deals currently pushed to FY2027 land and the Managed Services bookings decline reverses. The $9B FY2026 acquisition program (AI/data/cybersecurity) successfully compounds capability and cross-sell, and the realized savings from the ~22,000-role restructuring drop to margin instead of being fully reinvested, expanding EBITDA margin toward 18.5%+. Post-crash valuation (shares down >50% in 2026, EV/owner-FCF ~12x) already discounts most of the disruption fear, so re-rating adds further upside on top of fundamental recovery.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised above the 15% house default to 30% because the disruption thesis is a live, evidenced repricing event (an 18-20% single-day drop on a concrete bookings deterioration, not a hypothetical risk) and management itself cut guidance mid-year rather than defending the prior range -- this is closer to 'thesis materializing' than 'risk factor on the list'. Base weight trimmed to 45% (from the 50% default) because the range of plausible structural outcomes here is wide enough that no single path deserves outright majority confidence. Bull weight trimmed to 25% because it requires several things to go right simultaneously (large deals actually land in FY2027, Managed Services bookings decline reverses, and the accelerated $9B M&A program integrates cleanly) rather than a single catalyst.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
